text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000183 bills 99215 well above its risk-adjusted expectation in every complexity band, including low-complexity patients, but records came back for too few claims to test whether the notes support the billed levels.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern leans toward concern. The 99215 share runs roughly two to three times the all-provider rate in every complexity band, not only among sicker patients. A third of the 99215s fall on patients with zero or one chronic condition, often with simple diagnoses such as low back pain (C0107609, C0107790, C0107822), rash (C0107357) or follow-up encounter codes (C0107257, C0107751). The high-complexity sampled 99215s (e.g., C0108075, C0108623) look clinically plausible, and the overall mix is also shifted toward 99214, which could reflect either a sicker panel or systematic level inflation. The documentation cannot settle this: one supported 99215 (C0107774) and one 99214 documented at low MDM (C0107876), out of 7 charts, is far too thin to judge. A reviewer should first request records for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed here and check whether MDM and time genuinely support level 5, watching for cloned or templated notes."}
